hints: Look carefully at the two comparisons: right ventricle pressure is lower than the chamber before it (right atrium) and also lower than the vessel after it (pulmonary artery).
Remember valves are pushed open by higher pressure behind them and slammed shut by higher pressure in front of them to prevent backflow.
walkthrough:
**Recall how heart valves work**

Think of valves as one-way doors pushed by pressure. Blood always tries to flow from high pressure to low pressure.

If pressure behind the valve is higher, it pushes open. If pressure ahead is higher, it pushes shut.

**Check the atrioventricular valve on the right**

Here, right atrium pressure is higher than right ventricle pressure. So blood wants to flow forwards from atrium into ventricle.

That forward push opens the tricuspid atrioventricular valve.

**Check the semilunar valve on the right**

Here, pulmonary artery pressure is higher than right ventricle pressure. So blood would try to flow backwards into the ventricle.

That backward push closes the pulmonary semilunar valve to prevent backflow. Open AV and closed semilunar matches row C.

options.A: Both closed is wrong because higher atrial pressure would push the atrioventricular valve open to fill the ventricle.
options.B: This is backwards. Low ventricular pressure cannot open the semilunar valve against higher artery pressure, and it should allow the atrioventricular valve to open.
options.C: Correct. Higher atrium pressure opens the atrioventricular valve for filling, while higher artery pressure keeps the semilunar valve closed to stop backflow.
options.D: Both open is impossible here because the semilunar valve cannot be open when artery pressure is higher than ventricle pressure.
